reviews.evidence: Hausdorff–Young extends the L1 Fourier transform to Lp→Lq for 1≤p≤2; Lp space, Fourier transform, Haar measures, and equivalence classes are direct inputs.
The Hecke algebra is defined by compactly supported K-bi-invariant functions and Haar convolution; locally compact group, compact subgroup, Haar measure, and convolution are direct.
The conclusion is a band-limited L2 multiplier controlled by a radial growth condition; radial growth and bounded Fourier support are the reusable concepts needed to state the result.
The theorem assumes ball and line porosity and derives a Fourier concentration estimate; both porosity notions are direct hypotheses and no downstream uncertainty theorem is needed.
The construction takes a family of strongly continuous unitary representations on Hilbert spaces and forms their Hilbert direct sum; every listed prerequisite is used in the definition.
The transform is first defined on Schwartz functions by a principal-value integral and extended on L2 via Plancherel; Schwartz space, linear maps, and Plancherel are direct.
The identity compares unitary induction through H⊂K⊂G; locally compact groups, unitary representations, homogeneous spaces, and induced representations are direct.
The integrated form is the Haar integral of f(g)π(g) for f in the L1 group algebra; group, Haar measure, unitary representation, L1 algebra, and coefficient/operator action are used.
The operator-valued integral for compactly supported f uses Haar measure and Bochner integration in a Banach space; Banach, locally compact, convolution, and linear structure are direct.
The definition is a positive normalized translation-invariant functional on bounded functions; a topological group is the only ambient structure required.

The Jacquet module is coinvariants under the unipotent radical, with normalized action involving the parabolic modulus; local field, reductive/parabolic/Levi structure, smooth representation, and modulus are direct.
The L1 group algebra combines the L1 space with group convolution and involution; its listed prerequisites are the ingredients of the definition, including the modular correction.

The classification states irreducible admissible p-adic representations as unique quotients of normalized parabolic inductions; field, reductive group, parabolic/Levi data, admissibility, induction, temperedness, and characters are direct.
The result assumes line porosity and constructs a damping function with specified parameters; those two knowls are exactly the direct hypothesis and output definitions.

The space G/H is built from a closed subgroup's cosets with quotient topology and continuous action; subgroup, coset, quotient topology, action, and local compactness are direct, so subgroup/coset prerequisites were added.
The theorem classifies systems of imprimitivity for a transitive G-action as induced representations; system, transitive action, unitary representation, and locally compact group are direct.

The construction parametrizes irreducible representations of A⋊K from K-orbits in the dual and stabilizer representations; semidirect product, dual, stabilizer, and irreducible unitary representation are direct.

The definition uses reductive groups over nonarchimedean fields, valuation rings, profinite compactness, and group schemes to define hyperspecial maximal compacts; those structures are directly invoked.

The algebra consists of bounded regular complex Borel measures with product-measure pushforward convolution; Borel measure was added because it is a defining input, while product measure and Banach algebra remain direct.
The modular function is defined by right translation of a left Haar measure and is a continuous group homomorphism; Haar, right translation, homomorphism, and local compactness are direct.
Multiplicity is read from a type-I direct-integral decomposition over the unitary dual; direct integrals, measurable functions, a.e. classes, Hilbert spaces, and the dual are direct.
Normalized induction modifies ordinary parabolic induction by the square root of the parabolic modulus; reductive/parabolic/Levi/unipotent data, smooth representations, and modulus are direct.
The definition is an integral with complex phase e^{iλφ} and amplitude; complex numbers and Lebesgue integration are the only direct ingredients.
The equivalence relates L2 functions with bounded Fourier support to entire functions of exponential type; entire functions are the defining analytic target and Fourier/L2 notation is local.

The character is defined from determinant action on the Lie algebra of the unipotent radical; local field, reductive/parabolic/Levi/unipotent structure, character, Lie algebra, and modular action are direct.

Plancherel measure is characterized by decomposing the L2 Fourier transform into Hilbert–Schmidt operators over the unitary dual; Haar, dual, Hilbert–Schmidt, and unitary representation data are direct.

The theorem extends the LCA Fourier transform to a unitary L2 map and uses dual Haar normalization; abelian/local compact groups, Haar/dual measures, Fourier transform, unitary operators, Hilbert spaces, and inner products are direct.

The nonabelian Plancherel identity integrates Hilbert–Schmidt norms against Plancherel measure for a unimodular type-I group; each listed representation, measure, transform, and Hilbert prerequisite is used.
The proposition applies the higher-dimensional BM theorem to produce a plurisubharmonic majorant; radial growth, the BM theorem, and plurisubharmonic functions are direct.
Poisson extension convolves boundary data with the upper-half-plane Poisson kernel and produces a harmonic function; kernel and harmonic-function definitions are direct.
The kernel is the explicit positive normalized harmonic kernel on the upper half-plane; harmonic function is the only linked defining concept.
The dual is the group of continuous characters into the unit circle; local compactness, abelian groups, complex numbers, and homomorphisms are direct.
The theorem identifies G with its double dual via evaluation and asserts topological group isomorphism; dual, abelian/local compact groups, isomorphism, and homeomorphism are direct.
Positive definiteness is the nonnegative finite coefficient matrix condition for a continuous function on a topological group; topology and positive-semidefinite matrices are direct.
Quasi-invariance is mutual absolute continuity of every action pushforward with the reference measure; measurable spaces, measures, local compact group actions, and absolute continuity are direct.
The representation acts on Lp(G/H) using the Radon–Nikodym cocycle of a quasi-invariant measure; homogeneous spaces, quasi-invariance, Lp, and local compactness are direct.
The functional is defined by measurable radial rescaling and a weighted integral; no prerequisite is needed because the weight, supremum, and integral are introduced locally.
Left/right regular representations act on L2(G) using Haar measure, modular correction, and translations; Lp, Haar, modular function, strong representation, and right translation are direct.
Reiter P1 is a net of positive normalized L1 functions asymptotically invariant on compact sets; locally compact groups, Haar/L1 algebra, and translations are direct.
The restricted tensor product is indexed by completions of a number field and local Schwartz–Bruhat spaces with distinguished vectors; number field was added as a missing defining input.
